security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel or bhyve hypervisor hardcodes stale Smnip draft CSR addresses (msp at 0x348 instead of 0x349, ssp at 0x148 instead of 0x149, mithreshold at 0xFB1 instead of 0x347, sithreshold at 0x1B1 instead of 0x147) that were corrected by this spec errata. Hardware implementing the final spec will decode the old addresses as different CSRs (e.g., 0x348 is now mipreemptcfg, not msp), causing the kernel to read/write the wrong architectural state during context switch, trap entry/exit, or bhyve guest save/restore.
security_spec.summary: Smnip CSR address errata: FreeBSD kernel must use corrected addresses (msp=0x349, ssp=0x149, mithreshold=0x347, sithreshold=0x147) to avoid aliasing mipreemptcfg as msp and corrupting interrupt-priority state on context switch

findings.finding: FreeBSD RISC-V encoding.h has no Smnip CSR definitions at all — neither stale draft addresses (0x348, 0x148, 0xFB1, 0x1B1) nor correct final-spec addresses (0x346-0x349, 0x146-0x147, 0x149). The CSR definition table stops at CSR_SIP (0x144) and resumes at CSR_SATP (0x180); at M-level it stops at CSR_MIP (0x344) and resumes at CSR_PMPCFG0 (0x3a0). The stale-address violation condition is not met because no stale addresses are hardcoded.

findings.finding: Boot sequence (initriscv) has no Smnip configuration code — no references to any Smnip CSRs (stale or correct). The kernel does not attempt to read/write mithreshold, sithreshold, mspcs, sspcs, mipreemptcfg, mpistatus, or spistatus during boot.

findings.finding: Trap entry/exit paths contain no stale Smnip CSR address references. The kernel does not attempt to save/restore any Smnip state (mpistatus, spistatus, mipreemptcfg, mspcs, sspcs) during trap handling. No stale draft addresses are hardcoded.

findings.finding: Bhyve VMM code under sys/riscv/vmm/ contains zero references to any Smnip CSR addresses (stale or correct). No Smnip CSRs are virtualized for guests, but critically, no stale draft addresses are hardcoded that would cause the hypervisor to read/write the wrong architectural state.
